sentences.text: The genus Stromerosuchus and its single species, Stromerosuchus aegyptiacus, were both named by Oskar Kuhn in 1936.
The holotype specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — was gathered by Ernst Stromer and Richard Markgraf in 1911.
Unfortunately, the fossils collected by Stromer were badly crushed during shipment from Egypt to Germany.
Due to the poor quality of known remains, the genus Stromerosuchus is currently considered a nomen dubium, a term for a name of uncertain validity.
Some material previously assigned to Stromerosuchus has been reclassified into the genera Aegyptosuchus and Stomatosuchus.
The classification of Stromerosuchus has shifted over time, moving from Crocodylia to Stromerosuchidae, then to Aegyptosuchidae, and finally to Crocodyliformes.
Stromerosuchus is a dubious genus of crocodyliform that lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
Fossil remains of this animal have been found in the Cenomanian-age Bahariya Formation of Egypt.
